The sun hung low over the horizon, casting long shadows across the quiet street. A lone pigeon flapped its wings, searching for scraps in the alleyway. The air smelled of rain and damp earth, a reminder that summer had faded into autumn’s first whispers.

I sat on the bench, watching the world pass by—children laughing, a dog chasing its tail, a woman lost in thought. Life moved on, indifferent to the weight of my own thoughts. Sometimes, I wondered if anyone else felt the same way: the quiet ache of existence, the fleeting beauty of ordinary moments.

A gust of wind rustled the leaves, and I closed my eyes, letting the sound wash over me. For a moment, I was just a boy sitting on a bench, watching the world go by. And that was enough.
